acceptance: Quick promotion requires either mean development normalized-HV/AUC gain >=1 percent with no instance final-HV loss >0.02, or runtime gain >=10 percent with mean final-HV loss <=0.005 and no instance loss >0.02.
Intermediate accuracy acceptance requires normalized-HV gain >=0.005 or IGD+ reduction >=5 percent and satisfaction of every non-inferiority rule.

Intermediate efficiency acceptance requires runtime or time-to-95-HV improvement >=10 percent, normalized-HV loss <=0.005, IGD+ regression <=5 percent, feasible-rate loss <=0.03, and no lower feasible-archive success.

Final target requires rank 1 or tolerance-tied rank 1 on normalized-HV or IGD+, rank 1 or tolerance-tied rank 1 on runtime, time-to-95-HV, or NFE-to-95-HV, and mean rank <=4 on every required metric among seven algorithms.

Final target additionally requires Holm-adjusted significant superiority over at least three of six baselines and non-inferiority to every remaining baseline on the relevant winning accuracy and efficiency metrics; holdout and robustness must not reverse the conclusion.
allowed_regressions: Only regressions within the metric-specific non-inferiority tolerances are allowed; no constraint-success regression is allowed.
inconclusive: Evidence inside uncertainty/tolerance bands or with conflicting required metrics is INCONCLUSIVE; run only the next contract-permitted stage, otherwise reject without promotion.
invalid: Nonfinite objective or decision state, evaluator/schema error, unexplained NFE exceedance, persistent timeout/crash, protected-scope drift, fairness violation, benchmark special casing, or invalid-run fraction above 5 percent makes a candidate INVALID.
non_inferiority: normalized-HV paired aggregate loss no greater than 0.005
IGD+ paired aggregate regression no greater than 5 percent, or absolute 0.0001 when comparator is zero
runtime, time-to-95-HV, and NFE-to-95-HV regression no greater than 10 percent without lower hit rate
feasible-solution-rate loss no greater than 0.03 and no lower feasible-archive success

evaluation_stages.name: static
promotion_rules: Source inspection, import, unit tests, scope diff, and schema checks all pass without an objective call.

evaluation_stages.name: smoke
promotion_rules: This schema stage is the scientific quick screen: one initial-incumbent slot plus at most twelve candidates; apply the locked quick promotion rule. The separate 24000-NFE deterministic baseline smoke validation is charged to fixed_allowance.

evaluation_stages.name: quick
promotion_rules: This schema stage is the scientific intermediate screen: one initial-incumbent slot plus at most four candidates; apply accuracy or efficiency acceptance and every non-inferiority rule.

evaluation_stages.name: intermediate
promotion_rules: This schema stage is the scientific full-development gate: at most two frozen candidate finalists; select the incumbent before holdout is opened.

evaluation_stages.name: full
promotion_rules: Run the frozen ASH-MOSFMO and six frozen baselines; no algorithm modification after the first holdout execution; compute authoritative ranks and corrected tests.

evaluation_stages.name: robustness
promotion_rules: Run the same seven frozen algorithms and require that robustness does not reverse the final target conclusion.

extensions.checkpoint_semantics: A snapshot is taken after the first completed environmental-selection state at or beyond each 500-NFE boundary and labeled with actual NFE; final snapshot is always at the exact budget.
extensions.failure_semantics: Persistent run failure records normalized_hv=0, igd_plus=null with statistical penalty 10*sqrt(M), feasible rates 0, runtime=120 seconds for ranking, and consumes its attempted evaluations.
extensions.nondominated_ties: Exact duplicate objective vectors retain the earliest evaluation; crowding ties use stable evaluation order then decision-vector lexicographic order.
extensions.reference_normalization: For each frozen reference set, ideal=min per objective and nadir=max per objective; zero range is a fatal evaluator defect. Hypervolume reference point is 1.1 in every normalized objective.

fairness_constraints: Every comparable algorithm receives the same objective information, normalized-coordinate interface, initial sample for a paired instance-seed, strict NFE budget, archive capacity, checkpoint semantics, clipping, constraint convention, hardware, and thread limits.
All objective calls, including invalid candidates and initialization, consume NFE; no reference-front or known-optimum information is exposed to optimizers.
Population-based algorithms use nominal N=100; ASH-MOSFMO alone may reduce active N to the predeclared minimum 40 while retaining archive 100, because population reduction is the tested mechanism.
Boundary repair is coordinate-wise clipping in normalized [0,1]^D for all algorithms.
Constraint violation is sum(max(G_j,0)); Deb feasibility-first precedence applies before Pareto dominance or decomposition quality.
Runtime experiments use one process and one numerical thread; import, reference-front construction, metric post-processing, and serialization are excluded consistently.
Holdout instances are not executed before the final algorithm and its parameters are frozen.
Valid, failed, timed-out, and unfavorable runs are retained and reported.

metrics.aggregation: Per instance median and IQR over seeds; cross-instance mean rank with ties within 0.005.
metrics.meaning: Exact dominated hypervolume of the feasible nondominated archive after objective normalization, reference point 1.1 in every objective, divided by the frozen reference-front hypervolume and clipped to [0,1]. Empty feasible archive is zero.
metrics.name: normalized_hv
metrics.statistical_requirement: Final Friedman omnibus and Holm-adjusted paired Wilcoxon comparisons on per-instance medians.

metrics.acceptable_regression: 5 percent relative; when comparator median is zero use absolute 0.0001
metrics.aggregation: Per instance median and IQR over seeds; cross-instance mean rank with relative ties within 5 percent.
metrics.meaning: IGD+ from the frozen normalized reference front to the feasible nondominated archive; empty archive is +infinity, mapped to 10*sqrt(M) only for finite statistical computation.
metrics.name: igd_plus
metrics.statistical_requirement: Final Friedman omnibus and Holm-adjusted paired Wilcoxon comparisons on per-instance medians.

metrics.aggregation: Per instance median and IQR; cross-instance mean rank with relative ties within 10 percent.
metrics.meaning: perf_counter wall time for search, including algorithm bookkeeping, archive and sorting, excluding import, reference construction, post-hoc metrics, and serialization.
metrics.name: runtime_seconds
metrics.statistical_requirement: Paired fixed-order seeds, fixed single-thread environment, randomized algorithm run order, Friedman plus Holm-Wilcoxon at final.

metrics.acceptable_regression: 10 percent relative provided hit rate is not lower
metrics.aggregation: Lexicographic per instance: hit rate descending then median hit time ascending; cross-instance mean rank.
metrics.meaning: Search time at the first completed environmental-selection checkpoint with normalized HV >=0.95; a miss is right-censored at final runtime and ranked after every hit.
metrics.name: time_to_95_hv_seconds
metrics.statistical_requirement: Report censoring and hit rate; Holm-Wilcoxon uses paired finite hits only and cannot override a worse hit rate.

metrics.acceptable_regression: 10 percent relative provided hit rate is not lower
metrics.aggregation: Lexicographic per instance: hit rate descending then median hit NFE ascending; cross-instance mean rank.
metrics.meaning: Actual NFE at the first completed environmental-selection checkpoint with normalized HV >=0.95; a miss is right-censored at the run budget.
metrics.name: nfe_to_95_hv
metrics.statistical_requirement: Report censoring and paired seed outcomes.

metrics.aggregation: Median actual NFE and budget compliance rate.
metrics.meaning: Number of objective-vector evaluations, including failed candidate evaluations; ordinary completed full runs must equal the locked budget exactly.
metrics.name: evaluation_count
metrics.statistical_requirement: Any unexplained budget exceedance invalidates the run.

metrics.aggregation: Per constrained instance median and IQR; cross-constrained-instance mean rank with ties within 0.03.
metrics.meaning: Fraction of all evaluated points satisfying every G_j<=0; unconstrained problems report 1.0.
metrics.name: feasible_solution_rate
metrics.statistical_requirement: Report constrained instances separately and use final paired comparisons.

metrics.meaning: Whether the final archive contains at least one feasible solution.
metrics.name: feasible_archive_success
metrics.statistical_requirement: A lower success proportion defeats non-inferiority regardless of feasible_solution_rate.

metrics.aggregation: Per development instance median over seeds then mean rank.
metrics.meaning: Trapezoidal area under the normalized-HV versus NFE curve at completed environmental-selection checkpoints, divided by the run budget.
metrics.name: normalized_hv_auc
metrics.statistical_requirement: Used for quick-stage screening only, never as a replacement for final metrics.

problem.description: Two-to-five objective continuous minimization with finite box bounds and optional inequalities G(x)<=0; all algorithms operate internally in normalized [0,1]^D coordinates.

project.name: High-efficiency multi-objective Sheep Flock Migrate Optimization

repeated_runs.additional_run_policy: No discretionary additional seeds. One diagnostic retry of a transient failure may replace, but never add to, the stage allocation and its evaluations count against that allocation.
repeated_runs.policy: Nested fixed seeds: quick first 3, intermediate first 8, full first 20; robustness uses 10 disjoint unseen seeds.
repeated_runs.seed_selection: Fixed before observing any multi-objective result; holdout problems are unavailable to candidate decisions.

reproducibility.artifact_retention: Retain every valid, failed, timed-out, interrupted, and unfavorable structured result, log, hypothesis, candidate manifest, checksum, snapshot, and report under .autoresearch.
randomness_controls: numpy Generator seeded by the declared run seed
paired initialization generated once from the instance-seed and passed identically to each algorithm
reproducibility.source_version: Original sfmo.py SHA-256 and every protected/candidate implementation SHA-256; no pre-existing Git repository.

research_objective: Construct and validate an efficient, high-performing multi-objective SFMO that ranks first or tied-first on at least one accuracy metric and one efficiency metric, while ranking fourth or better among seven algorithms on every required metric.
risks: archive and nondominated-sorting overhead dominating cheap objective runtime
unfair comparator weakening from implementation errors
constraint difficulty causing empty feasible archives
success-history feedback collapsing to a narrow behavior mode

allowed_change_kinds: linear or state-aware active population reduction from 100 to no fewer than 40
external archive and diversity-preserving leader selection
sheep flock fission-fusion, grazing, migration, regrouping, and alarm-inspired operators
rank-biased mentorship and unsuccessful-experience archive inspired by RDE mechanisms
implementation optimization that preserves evaluator semantics
forbidden_change_kinds: editing the locked contract or protected benchmark semantics
benchmark, instance, seed, known optimum, or reference-front special casing
changing metrics, seeds, budgets, tolerances, baselines, or acceptance rules
candidate-only extra evaluations or hidden objective calls

methods: Friedman rank test across problem-instance median blocks
paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc tests
paired hierarchical bootstrap over problem then seed for 95 percent effect intervals
median, IQR, mean rank, and win-tie-loss reporting
statistical_protocol.minimum_evidence: Quick uses 3 seeds on 6 development instances; intermediate uses 8; authoritative full uses 20 seeds on all 12 development/holdout instances; robustness uses 10 unseen seeds.
statistical_protocol.multiplicity: Holm family-wise correction at alpha 0.05 across ASH-MOSFMO versus six baselines for each final primary metric; no uncorrected claim is authoritative.
statistical_protocol.pairing: The same fixed seed is paired across algorithms for an instance; final hypothesis-test blocks are the twelve independent instance medians.
statistical_protocol.uncertainty_reporting: Median and IQR per instance plus deterministic 10000-resample hierarchical bootstrap 95 percent intervals using analysis RNG seed 424242.

stopping_rules.budget_exhaustion: Stop when 51108000 objective-vector evaluations or 86400 seconds of active experiment wall time is exhausted; do not borrow between stages beyond their candidate slots.
other_terminal_conditions: unrecoverable external dependency or environment block
persistent invalid-run rate above the locked threshold
stagnation: Stop candidate generation after four consecutive valid candidates fail to replace the incumbent.
target_conditions: All final acceptance conditions, statistical requirements, rank requirements, holdout checks, and robustness checks pass.

uncertainties: There is no unique published multi-objective SFMO reference, so the initial MO-SFMO is a frozen minimal archive-based extension documented in code.
MOPIO variants differ in the literature; the exact protected archive-grid adaptation and parameters declared here define the comparator.
Absolute timing variance on a shared Windows workstation may be higher than objective-evaluation variance.
